steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The contexts of British cinema — social, cultural and political — are distinct from those of Hollywood and must be understood on their own terms to analyse UK film meaningfully.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Post-war British cinema was shaped by the austerity of reconstruction, the birth of the welfare state and the emergence of social realism as a response to the failures and promises of post-war recovery.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The British New Wave of the late 1950s and 1960s emerged from a cultural context of class consciousness, industrial change and the influence of European art cinema and Documentary Film Movement traditions.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Thatcherism in the 1980s profoundly reshaped British society through privatisation, deindustrialisation and the attack on trade unions, generating both the social conditions that films depicted and the political anger that fuelled filmmakers.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: How did Thatcherism shape the context of British cinema in the 1980s and beyond? | Q: What was the significance of the British New Wave for UK cinema? | Q: How has post-colonial multicultural Britain influenced the themes and representations of UK film?

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always connect contextual knowledge to specific moments, choices and meanings in the film — never discuss context in isolation. Identify which contexts are most relevant to your film: social, cultural and political contexts interact but some are more significant than others for each film. Use British-specific contextual terminology — Thatcherism, devolution, austerity, post-war reconstruction — rather than vague references to 'the time period'. Consider how the film's context of production differs from the context it depicts — many British films are set in an earlier period but shaped by contemporary concerns. Explain how context affects meaning for audiences: the same film would carry different significance for viewers in different political or social moments.
